Purpose: Recreate the interaction philosophy and visual language of a temporary, keyboard-first scratchpad.
Product philosophy
The application is a transient writing workspace, not a knowledge-management system. It should appear instantly, accept typing without setup, and disappear just as quickly.

The editor must remain the visual centerpiece. Organization, utilities, and preferences should stay secondary.
Window and layout
Main editor

* One rounded, floating, resizable window.
* Minimal title/action bar with unobtrusive controls.
* Entire main surface functions as the editor.
* Wide enough for short notes and calculations, without the density of a full IDE.
* No permanent sidebar, ribbon, formatting toolbar, or document tabs.
* Optional small status/date/note-count indicators.
* Independent caret and scroll-position restoration for each note.
Reference-only proposed dimensions: 440 × 540 logical pixels initially, with user resizing. These are implementation targets, not confirmed Antinote measurements.

Alternative surfaces

* Normal desktop window.
* Menu-bar/dropdown presentation.
* Pinned always-on-top presentation.
* Split view containing an ephemeral note and one permanent slotted note.
Visual system
Typography
* Monospaced text as the primary editor font.
* Proposed 14–16 px default size with scalable text.
* Approximately 1.4× line height.
* Three levels of textual hierarchy: editor content, semantic emphasized content, subtle metadata.
Color roles

Maintain distinct theme variables for:

* Background and window chrome.
* Foreground and muted text.
* Mode keywords.
* Variables and syntax identifiers.
* Numbers and computed results.
* Links and selections.
* Completed checklist items.
* Errors and confirmation states.
* Paper textures and caret.
Do not use one accent color for all syntax types.

Surface customization

* Separate light and dark palettes.
* Blank, lined, dotted, small-grid and large-grid paper.
* Subtle, clear and bold pattern strength.
* Native translucent window material where available.
* Independent themes for split-view panes.
* High-contrast and opaque fallback modes.
Core UX flows
Quick capture

1. Invoke the global hotkey.
2. Display the current or a new scratchpad.
3. Restore keyboard focus immediately.
4. Type and autosave continuously.
5. Dismiss without interrupting the user's previous application.
Note navigation

* Two-finger horizontal swipe traverses the ephemeral stack.
* Moving beyond the newest note creates a new note.
* Abandoned empty notes disappear.
* Keyboard shortcuts provide equivalent navigation.
* Notes can be promoted, deleted, searched, and reordered.
* Deleted nonempty notes go into recoverable trash.
Search
* Open a compact temporary search surface.
* Filter notes as the user types.
* Present compact list and card-grid display choices.
* Allow keyboard selection and immediate opening.
* Support batch operations and drag reorder.
* Keep search navigation separate from the primary editor.
Permanent slots
* Nine fixed notes exist alongside the ephemeral stack.
* A floating bottom bar allows switching between slots.
* Slots never expire; deleting their content clears the slot.
* Split view shows one slot alongside an ephemeral note.
* The floating slot selector can fade when inactive.
Editor behavior
Plain text: Direct editable text with minimal formatting interference.

Lists: Automatic interactive checkboxes, bullets and numbered lists. Support nested items, checked-state styling, keyboard toggles, and continuing lists on Return.
Math: A first-line keyword activates inline calculations, variables, unit conversions, and colored computed answers.
Code: A first-line keyword such as code: py enables syntax highlighting. Preserve code indentation and raw text. This is a scratch snippet editor, not a full IDE.
Markdown: Recognize headings, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, inline/fenced code and comments without introducing a formatting ribbon.
Links: Shorten long displayed URLs while retaining their original underlying text and clipboard representation.
Commands: Contextual keyword or extension completion should appear near the caret, with the relevant command description and arguments.
Utilities: Timer, OCR and automatic clipboard capture remain integrated into the same writing environment.
Feedback and animations
Animations should communicate action without delaying it.
Proposed targets:

* Open/close: approximately 100–170 ms.
* Horizontal note navigation: approximately 160–230 ms.
* Small hover feedback: less than 100 ms.
* Search filtering: visually immediate.
* Checkbox toggling: immediate update with subtle status styling.
* Reduced-motion mode: disable decorative transforms.
These values are engineering proposals; actual Antinote timing is not verified.
Accessibility and reliability
* Complete keyboard navigation.
* Customizable system-wide shortcut.
* Clear focus and selection states.
* Proper screen reader labels.
* High-DPI and mixed-monitor support.
* Multilingual text input and IME compatibility.
* Reduced-motion and high-contrast support.
* Per-note undo/redo.
* Reliable autosave and crash recovery.
* No focus stealing while the scratchpad is hidden.
UX acceptance criteria
A successful implementation should make the following possible:

1. Capture a note without clicking a single control.
2. Navigate and create notes without opening a menu.
3. Enter and dismiss the window without losing focus or text.
4. Render Markdown and syntax colors without cursor misalignment.
5. Resize, change themes and use translucency without breaking readability.
6. Search and restore notes without exposing permanent organizational clutter.
7. Keep application resource consumption minimal while hidden.
Platform-specific adaptation: On Windows, use native window/backdrop capabilities and appropriate Windows shortcuts. Do not reproduce macOS traffic lights or Liquid Glass literally when platform-native equivalents provide a better result.
